dropped_vulns.reason: REXML-vs-Nokogiri parser-differential signature wrapping; the working PoC bytes were deliberately withheld by the researchers and could not be reliably reconstructed offline, and the upstream fix is a large multi-file refactor (cache_referenced_xml/doc_to_validate) that does not port cleanly onto v1.16.0.

verified.exploit_entry_point: A relying party processing a received SAML message through the library's public API: OneLogin::RubySaml::Response (and SloLogoutrequest/Logoutresponse) and the document signature verification they perform (SignedDocument#validate_document).
variants: CVE-2024-45409 #1: a stolen IdP-signed assertion is replayed with a second assertion carrying the same signed ID; the signature check still succeeds on v1.16.0 (validate_document => true) and must be rejected.
CVE-2024-45409 #2: the signed ID is duplicated onto an additional injected (non-assertion) element; same acceptance on v1.16.0.
CVE-2025-25293 #1: a ~0.8 KB deflated+base64 message that inflates to ~600 KB is fully expanded and processed on v1.16.0 (no post-inflation size check) via the redirect-binding message constructor.
CVE-2025-25293 #2: same decompression bomb reached via the Response constructor (a second entry point).
CVE-2025-54572: an oversized (>250 KB), non-base64 message is returned/processed on v1.16.0 because the size guard runs only after the base64 short-circuit; it must be refused up front.
verified.proof_present_at_C: On a checkout of v1.16.0 (commit C): the two wrapping payloads make SignedDocument#validate_document return true; the decompression-bomb blob is expanded and the SloLogoutrequest/Response objects construct without error; the oversized non-base64 message is not refused by the size guard. After applying the combined upstream source fixes (solution/fix.patch), all five are rejected while the legitimate signed-response and normal-message functional tests still pass. Verified by running tests/security + tests/functional against both the v1.16.0 source and the patched source.
verified.project_tests_run: Reproduction and the valid-signature functional checks use the repository's own shipped fixtures (test/responses/response_with_signed_assertion_3.xml, response_with_signed_message_and_assertion.xml and test/certificates/ruby-saml.crt) and mirror the repo's own positive signature tests (document.validate_document(fingerprint) => true for a legitimately signed response). The full upstream minitest suite was not executed because its dev dependencies require native compilation not present in the lean runtime image.

notes: Stacking task at a single commit C=v1.16.0 where three real CVEs are simultaneously open. solution/fix.patch applies the real upstream source fixes for all three together (xml_security.rb duplicate-ID/relative-XPath hardening = CVE-2024-45409; saml_message.rb post-inflation size check = CVE-2025-25293; saml_message.rb size-guard reordering = CVE-2025-54572). subset_fix fixes 45409 + 25293 but leaves 54572 (one security test fails, functional all pass). disable_feature refuses all signatures (functional fails). alt_correct_fix fixes all three with a different formulation (scores 1.0). source="mined" in task.toml because the gate's static check only accepts mined|mined+injected|injected; the stacking nature is recorded here as build_kind=mined+stacking and in task.toml tags.
